answer: Yes, that's expected. The current dispatcher passes only the first captured value to `run`. The workaround is to capture the whole suffix in one group and parse it inside the callback. For example, use `pattern = "lookup:(.+)"` with `run = function(suffix) local kind, id = suffix:match("([^:]+):(.+)") ... end`. The source is Virtual Pages.md.

[1] Virtual Pages.md (How it works)
  Multiple capture groups: The current dispatcher passes only the first match value to `run`. If you need several values, capture the complete suffix and parse it inside the callback: / ```lua / virtualPage.define { / pattern = "lookup:(.+)", / run = function(suffix) / local kind, id = suffix:match("([^:]+):(.+)") / if not kind then return "Use lookup:kind:id" end / return "# " .. kind .. "\nLooking up: " .. id / end / } / ```
  How it works: You define a virtual page by calling `virtualPage.define` with a Lua pattern and a function. When someone navigates to a page name matching the pattern, SilverBullet calls your function instead of loading a file from disk. / The current standard-library dispatcher passes the first captured value from the pattern to the function. The function returns the Markdown content to display. Put definitions in a `space-lua` block in your own space, then run `System: Reload`. / ```lua / virtualPage.define { / pattern = "greeting:(.+)", / run = function(name) / return "# Hello, " .. name .. "!\nWelcome to this virtual page." / end / } / ``` / Navigating to `greeting:World` renders a page with the heading “Hello, World!” — but no file is created. / Virtual pages are always **read-only**. The editor disables editing controls automatically.
  - The standard library's event listener checks all registered patterns against the page name, and a matching `run` function's return value becomes the page content with read-only permissions.
  - A virtual page is defined by calling `virtualPage.define` with a Lua pattern and a function.
  - The current standard-library dispatcher passes the first captured value from the pattern to the function.
[2] CHANGELOG.md (CHANGELOG)
  2.10.0: * Fix: Space Lua now correctly truncates a parenthesized expression to a single value (Lua 5.4 semantics). Previously `(string.gsub(...))` and other parenthesized multi-return calls leaked their extra return values into `return`, call-argument, and assignment positions (e.g. `table.insert(t, (string.gsub(...)))` inserted two elements). Parentheses now yield exactly one value. / * Fix: Lua pattern matching lost capture groups, because `ipairs` dropped `nil` values from the result table (by [henrikx](https://github.com/henrikx)). / * Fix: `lintObjects` threw when a page’s `pageMeta` was undefined (by [josh-j](https://github.com/josh-j)). / * Fix: `mq.poll` materialized the entire queue on every poll (by [josh-j](https://github.com/josh-j)).
[3] API/capture.md (Example)
  - The capture.readFile and capture.saveFile functions only work inside the run function of the capture action that is running.
  - Each capture action is defined with a service.define call that has a match function and a run function.
Exact facts:
- [1] The most commonly used virtual pages are **tag pages**. When you click a hashtag like `#project`, SilverBullet navigates to `tag:project`, which is a virtual page that lists all objects with that tag — grouped by type (pages, tasks, items, data, etc.).
- [1] Tag pages are defined in the standard library and work out of the box. You can override the default tag page by defining your own `virtualPage.define` with the pattern `tag:(.+)`.
